channel.title: WEALTHMETER.XYZ Longform Feed
channel.description: Recent WealthMeter longform analysis on balance-sheet structure, resilience, and capital planning.

item.title: The Liquidity Illusion
item.description: Why household net worth, borrowing access, and practical cash resilience diverge once real conversion haircuts, deadlines, and refinancing dependence are measured directly.

item.title: The Yield Trap in a High-Rate World
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why headline yield can rise while real household resilience falls, and how investors misprice duration, credit, tax, and liquidity risk when income becomes the only target.

item.title: The Windfall Misallocation Problem
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why inheritances, equity payouts, business exits, and other windfalls are often allocated badly because recipients confuse one-time liquidity with durable balance-sheet strength.

item.title: The Wealth Plateau Effect
item.description: Why many households stop converting income into durable, optional wealth once assets become illiquid, contribution rates flatten, and lifestyle obligations start absorbing each new dollar of margin.

item.title: The War Premium: How the Iran Conflict Is Repricing Energy, Credit, and Equities
item.description: Data-enriched analysis of how Iran conflict risk is repricing oil, inflation, credit spreads, and equity valuations.

item.title: The Venture Capital Power Law Reality
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why venture capital outcomes follow a power law, why that concentrates return into a tiny slice of funds and deals, and what that means for household allocation discipline.

item.title: The Urban Premium Collapse
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why major-city income advantages no longer convert into the same after-housing, after-tax, after-time wealth premium they once did.

item.title: The Timing Fallacy in Public Markets
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why market timing fails for most households, how behavioral flow patterns destroy realized returns, and what disciplined public-market participation looks like instead.

item.title: The Skill Obsolescence Curve
item.description: Why career wealth fails when the market value of a worker skill stack decays faster than retraining, bargaining power, or liquidity can keep up.

item.title: The Second-Home Wealth Drain
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why second homes often weaken household balance sheets through duplicated carry, tax friction, underused capital, and false investment logic.

item.title: The Scarcity Mindset Loop
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of how scarcity thinking can survive rising income, compress time horizon, distort risk-taking, and keep households poorer in behavior than they are on paper.

item.title: The Salary Ceiling Illusion
item.description: A 2026 WealthMeter analysis of why high salary can still be a narrow wealth lane, how taxes and fixed costs compress real conversion, and why labor income often tops out before households expect.

item.title: The Risk Tolerance Illusion
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why stated risk tolerance usually measures mood and recent market experience more than true balance-sheet capacity, and what a decision-grade risk framework looks like instead.

item.title: Are You Rich or Just in a Bubble? Recalculating Wealth in a 6% Mortgage World
item.description: A practical framework for recalculating wealth in a 6% mortgage regime, where paper gains and real optionality can diverge.

item.title: The Rich but Not Famous Economy
item.description: Why much of modern wealth sits with business owners, executives, partners, and quiet capital allocators whose income and asset position are real but socially under-recognized.

item.title: The Retirement Age Lie
item.description: stress-testing retirement target numbers under current inflation, rate, and longevity conditions.

item.title: The Rent vs Buy Reversal
item.description: A 2026 refresh on why the rent-versus-buy decision now turns on financing cost, owner carry, tenure, and mobility value rather than on the old automatic ownership script.

item.title: The Rebalancing Illusion
item.description: Why rebalancing is not automatic wealth magic, where it truly helps, and how taxes, spreads, behavior, and weak policy design turn a good principle into an illusion.

item.title: Realistic Projections on UBI (Universal Basic Income): Don’t Bet Your Future on It
item.description: Evidence-based analysis of UBI timelines, pilot outcomes, fiscal realities, and why households should not assume near-term guaranteed income.

item.title: The Property Tax Drag
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why property tax is not a side expense but a recurring carry cost that changes affordability, retirement durability, and the real value of home equity.

item.title: The Promotion Paradox
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why career promotions often increase status and gross income while weakening net surplus, mobility, and long-run wealth conversion.

item.title: The Productivity-Income Disconnect
item.description: A 2026 WealthMeter analysis of why productivity gains do not translate cleanly into household income, and why workers should treat that gap as a planning constraint rather than an abstract macro debate.

item.title: The Private Markets Mirage
item.description: Why private-market prestige often exceeds private-market net investor economics, and why access, valuation lag, fee dispersion, and lockup risk matter more than the exclusivity story.

item.title: The Overconfidence Cycle
item.description: Why overconfidence behaves like a wealth process rather than a simple bias: gains get misread as skill, risk limits loosen, concentration rises, and the next mistake becomes larger.

item.title: The Opportunity Cost of Cash
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of when holding cash is prudent, when it becomes expensive, and how to judge the real opportunity cost by comparing liquidity value, inflation drag, and available after-tax return elsewhere.

item.title: One Salary, Three Futures: How the Same Income Produces Totally Different Wealth Paths by City
item.description: Why equal salaries produce different long-term wealth outcomes once city-level housing, taxes, and recurring costs are modeled.

item.title: The New Middle-Class Trap: High Income, Low Net Worth
item.description: Why high income can coexist with weak net-worth durability, and how to improve conversion from cash flow into resilience.

item.title: The Mortgage Lock-In Trap: Why a 3% Loan Can Still Make You Poorer in 2026
item.description: A practical WealthMeter analysis of mortgage lock-in in 2026: why a low fixed rate can preserve monthly cash flow while still reducing mobility, optionality, and real household wealth.

item.title: The Mobility Premium
item.description: Why the ability to move across jobs, cities, and housing structures behaves like a real wealth premium even when it does not appear on a balance sheet.

item.title: The Loss Aversion Tax
item.description: Why loss aversion behaves like a hidden tax on wealth: it distorts selling discipline, raises friction, delays reallocation, and keeps capital trapped in weaker uses.

item.title: Longevity Capital: Living to 120
item.description: how potential lifespan extension changes long-horizon wealth architecture.

item.title: The Lifestyle Lock-In Curve
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of how rising fixed-cost lifestyles capture future income, reduce optionality, and turn comfort upgrades into a curve of growing balance-sheet rigidity.

item.title: Inside Wealth: Germany, Japan, and Canada
item.description: structural comparison of top wealth outcomes in Germany, Japan, and Canada.

item.title: Inside Wealth in China and India: Top 10%, Top 1%, and the New Middle Class
item.description: A practical breakdown of top-10 and top-1 wealth dynamics in China and India, and what they reveal about modern middle-class resilience.

item.title: The Inheritance Illusion
item.description: why receiving wealth does not automatically create durable wealth outcomes.

item.title: The Inflation Ladder Problem
item.description: Why inflation hits household wealth through a reset ladder: cash loses purchasing power immediately, contracts update on different schedules, and nominal ladders can fail long before net worth screens show stress.

item.title: The Indexing Saturation Problem
item.description: Why the indexing boom still makes sense for households, where saturation risks actually appear, and why the real problem is benchmark concentration and thinner price-setting at the margin rather than market collapse.

item.title: The Illiquidity Premium Myth
item.description: Why the promise of extra return for locking up capital is often overstated, mismeasured, or consumed by fees, leverage, stale marks, and the option value of liquidity.

item.title: The 2026 Housing Stall: Rates, Inventory, and the New Delinquency Split
item.description: Why 2026 housing data looks better at the margin yet still supports a weak-turnover, uneven-stress housing regime.

item.title: The Hidden Costs of Ownership
item.description: Why houses, cars, second properties, and other owned assets often consume more cash, time, and strategic freedom than headline purchase prices suggest.

item.title: The Great Baseline War: Why Your Wealth Rank Changes by Population Lens
item.description: Why your wealth percentile shifts across global, national, local, and life-stage baselines, and how to use each lens correctly.

item.title: The Golden Handcuffs Equation
item.description: Why high compensation can still reduce strategic freedom when equity vesting, deferred pay, insurance dependence, and concentration risk make leaving expensive.

item.title: The Global Housing Divergence
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why housing markets no longer move as one trade, and how rates, supply, demographics, and policy create widening country-by-country and city-by-city divergence.

item.title: The Geographic Arbitrage Window
item.description: Why the best geographic arbitrage opportunities come from a temporary spread between earning power and local cost structure, and why that spread narrows once housing, tax, and labor markets catch up.

item.title: The Freelance Freedom Tradeoff
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why freelance work can expand autonomy while weakening insurance, retirement automation, income stability, and the surplus needed for durable wealth building.

item.title: The Equity Compensation Trap
item.description: RSU, ISO, and ESPP concentration risk and tax leakage in household wealth outcomes.

item.title: The End of the Safe Job Illusion: AI Labor Deflation in White-Collar Income
item.description: How AI is compressing white-collar compensation, fragmenting roles, and destabilizing career and household financial planning.

item.title: The Dual-Income Trap
item.description: why two salaries often underperform one salary in long-run wealth resilience.

item.title: The Debt Illusion Cycle
item.description: A WealthMeter analysis of why debt feels like wealth during expansion, how fixed obligations compound fragility, and where productive leverage differs from household self-deception.

item.title: Crypto ETF Wealth Effect: Durable Net Worth or Volatility?
item.description: How to evaluate whether crypto ETF gains are compounding into durable wealth or simply increasing cycle sensitivity.
